+def primus_record(level: str, where: str, message: str) -> str:
+    """A record of Primus's console logger, colour codes included: a multi-line
+    message runs on unprefixed lines up to the reset."""
+    return (
+        f"[\x1b[32m20261021 05:06:54\x1b[0m][\x1b[36mrank-0/8\x1b[0m]\x1b[1m{f'[{level}]':<11}\x1b[0m"
+        f"\x1b[1m[-------{where}] : {message}\x1b[0m\n"
+    )
+
+
+# Trimmed from a v26.9 rc1 Megatron-Bridge failure: a patch skipped for a
+# missing dependency logs an ImportError traceback first; the run then stops
+# on a bare AssertionError, which Primus wraps and torchrun summarizes.
+RC1_BRIDGE_FAILURE = (
+    primus_record(
+        "ERROR",
+        "patch_runner.py:132",
+        "[Patch] ✗ Patch 'megatron.turbo.te_spec_provider' failed due to missing dependency: "
+        "cannot import name 'TEGroupedMLPSubmodules' from 'megatron.core.transformer.moe.experts'\n"
+        "Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
+        '  File "/primus/core/patches/patch_runner.py", line 127, in run_patches\n'
+        "    patch.apply(ctx)\n"
+        "ImportError: cannot import name 'TEGroupedMLPSubmodules' from 'megatron.core.transformer.moe.experts'\n",
+    )
+    + primus_record("INFO", "train_runtime.py:559", "Python GC re-enabled after training")
+    + primus_record("ERROR", "traceback.py:1050", "Traceback (most recent call last):\n")
+    + primus_record(
+        "ERROR",
+        "traceback.py:1050",
+        '  File "/primus/core/runtime/train_runtime.py", line 108, in run_train_module\n'
+        "    self._initialize_backend_and_execute()\n",
+    )
+    + primus_record(
+        "ERROR",
+        "traceback.py:1050",
+        '  File "/Megatron-LM/megatron/core/optimizer_param_scheduler.py", line 74, in __init__\n'
+        "    assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps\n"
+        "           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^\n",
+    )
+    + primus_record("ERROR", "traceback.py:1050", "AssertionError\n")
+    + primus_record(
+        "ERROR",
+        "traceback.py:1050",
+        "\nThe above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:\n\n",
+    )
+    + primus_record("ERROR", "traceback.py:1050", "Traceback (most recent call last):\n")
+    + primus_record(
+        "ERROR",
+        "traceback.py:1050",
+        '  File "/primus/core/runtime/train_runtime.py", line 121, in run_train_module\n'
+        '    raise RuntimeError(f"Training execution failed: {e}") from e\n',
+    )
+    + primus_record("ERROR", "traceback.py:1050", "RuntimeError: Training execution failed: \n")
+    + primus_record(
+        "ERROR",
+        "__main__.py:220",
+        "[Primus] Error: RuntimeError: Training execution failed:  (/primus/core/runtime/train_runtime.py:121)",
+    )
+    + "E1021 05:06:59.430000 1586 torch/distributed/elastic/multiprocessing/api.py:1007] failed (exitcode: 1) "
+    "local_rank: 5 (pid: 1758) of binary: /opt/venv/bin/python3\n"
+    "Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
+    '  File "/opt/venv/bin/torchrun", line 10, in <module>\n'
+    "    sys.exit(main())\n"
+    "torch.distributed.elastic.multiprocessing.errors.ChildFailedError: \n"
+    "============================================================\n"
+    "primus/cli/main.py FAILED\n"
+    "[2026-10-21 05:06:59] [NODE-0(node)] [ERROR] [direct] torchrun exited with code 1\n"
+)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("colored", [True, False], ids=["colored", "no-colors"])
+def test_the_exception_that_stopped_the_run_is_the_detail(tmp_path, colored):
+    body = RC1_BRIDGE_FAILURE if colored else extract.strip_ansi(RC1_BRIDGE_FAILURE)
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(
+        str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=1, failure_reason="exit: launcher exited with code 1"))
+    )
+    assert (result["status"], result["failure_reason"]) == ("failed", "python_error")
+    assert result["failure_detail"] == (
+        "AssertionError: assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps (optimizer_param_scheduler.py:74)"
+    )
+    assert result["failed_at"] == "setup"
+
+
+def _traceback(*frames_then_exception: str) -> str:
+    *frames, exception = frames_then_exception
+    lines = ["Traceback (most recent call last):"]
+    for frame in frames:
+        lines += [f'  File "/src/{frame}.py", line 7, in {frame}', f"    {frame}()"]
+    return "\n".join(lines + [exception]) + "\n"
+
+
+CAUSE = "\nThe above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:\n\n"
+CONTEXT = "\nDuring handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:\n\n"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "body,reason,detail",
+    [
+        pytest.param(
+            _traceback("load", "KeyError: 'lr'")
+            + CAUSE
+            + _traceback("setup", "ValueError: the config has no lr"),
+            "python_error",
+            "KeyError: 'lr'",
+            id="raise-from-goes-to-the-cause",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            _traceback("load", "KeyError: 'lr'")
+            + CONTEXT
+            + _traceback("setup", "ValueError: the config has no lr"),
+            "python_error",
+            "ValueError: the config has no lr",
+            id="an-error-while-handling-one-is-the-new-error",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            _traceback("probe", "ImportError: optional apex")
+            + "training...\n"
+            + _traceback("step", "ValueError: bad"),
+            "python_error",
+            "ValueError: bad",
+            id="a-logged-traceback-before-the-fatal-one",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            _traceback("step", "torch.distributed.DistBackendError: NCCL error in: ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1234")
+            + CAUSE
+            + _traceback(
+                "train", "RuntimeError: Training execution failed: NCCL error in: ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1234"
+            ),
+            "nccl_error",
+            "torch.distributed.DistBackendError: NCCL error in: ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1234",
+            id="an-nccl-root-cause",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            _traceback("step", "ValueError: bad") + _traceback("main", "ChildFailedError: "),
+            "python_error",
+            "ValueError: bad",
+            id="torchrun-summary-is-not-the-cause",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            "".join(f"[rank3]: {line}\n" for line in _traceback("step", "ValueError: bad").splitlines()),
+            "python_error",
+            "ValueError: bad",
+            id="torch-rank-prefix",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            _traceback("load", "KeyError: 'lr'\nsee the recipe's optimizer section")
+            + CAUSE
+            + _traceback("setup", "ValueError: the config has no lr"),
+            "python_error",
+            "KeyError: 'lr'",
+            id="multi-line-message-before-the-link",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            "Root Cause (first observed failure):\n[0]:\n  rank      : 5 (local_rank: 5)\n"
+            "  traceback : Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
+            '    File "/src/sched.py", line 74, in __init__\n'
+            "      assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps\n"
+            "  AssertionError\n"
+            "============================================================\n",
+            "python_error",
+            "AssertionError: assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps (sched.py:74)",
+            id="torchrun-summary-with-an-error-file",
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_traceback_chains(tmp_path, body, reason, detail):
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=1)))
+    assert (result["failure_reason"], result["failure_detail"]) == (reason, detail)
+
+
+def test_another_ranks_lines_inside_a_traceback_are_skipped(tmp_path):
+    body = (
+        primus_record("ERROR", "traceback.py:1050", "Traceback (most recent call last):\n")
+        + primus_record("ERROR", "traceback.py:1050", '  File "/src/a.py", line 3, in f\n    g()\n')
+        + primus_record("INFO", "training.py:9", "iteration 3/20").replace("rank-0/8", "rank-7/8")
+        + "W1021 05:06:58.801000 1586 torch/distributed/elastic/multiprocessing/api.py:1033] Sending process 17 closing signal SIGTERM\n"
+        + primus_record("ERROR", "traceback.py:1050", "ValueError: bad shard\n")
+        + primus_record("ERROR", "__main__.py:220", "[Primus] Error: ValueError: bad shard (/src/a.py:3)")
+    )
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=1)))
+    assert (result["failure_reason"], result["failure_detail"]) == ("python_error", "ValueError: bad shard")
+
+
+def test_an_uncoloured_patch_message_does_not_hide_what_follows(tmp_path):
+    body = extract.strip_ansi(
+        primus_record("INFO", "patch_runner.py:126", "[Patch] Applying maxdiffusion.te_preload: preload TF")
+    ) + ("Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault\n" + _traceback("load", "RuntimeError: died"))
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=139)))

+def test_a_loguru_traceback_is_read(tmp_path):
+    body = (
+        "Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
+        '> File "/src/train.py", line 12, in <module>\n'

+def test_nccl_text_still_beats_a_generic_exception(tmp_path):
+    body = "[Rank 0] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(OpType=ALLREDUCE)\n" + _traceback(
+        "step", "RuntimeError: Rank 0 received an exception from rank 7"
+    )
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=1)))
+    assert result["failure_reason"] == "nccl_error"
+    assert result["failure_detail"].startswith("Watchdog caught collective operation timeout")
+
+
+def test_a_bare_exception_other_than_assert_gets_its_location_only(tmp_path):
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(
+        str(write_log(tmp_path, _traceback("next_batch", "StopIteration"), exit_code=1))

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("colored", [True, False], ids=["colored", "no-colors"])
+def test_a_patch_messages_chained_traceback_is_noise_too(tmp_path, colored):
+    patch = primus_record(
+        "ERROR",
+        "patch_runner.py:132",
+        "[Patch] ✗ Patch 'x' failed due to missing dependency: need triton\n"
+        + _traceback("probe", "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'triton'")
+        + CAUSE
+        + _traceback("patch", "ImportError: need triton"),
+    )
+    body = (patch if colored else extract.strip_ansi(patch)) + _traceback("step", "ValueError: bad shard")
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=1)))
+    assert result["failure_detail"] == "ValueError: bad shard"
+
+
+def test_a_link_line_only_joins_the_traceback_right_after_it(tmp_path):
+    body = (
+        _traceback("probe", "ValueError: caught and logged")
+        + CAUSE
+        + "training resumed\n"
+        + _traceback("step", "RuntimeError: the real crash")
+    )
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=1)))
+    assert result["failure_detail"] == "RuntimeError: the real crash"
+

+def test_a_c10_warning_inside_a_rank_traceback_is_skipped(tmp_path):
+    lines = [
+        "Traceback (most recent call last):",
+        '  File "/src/sched.py", line 74, in __init__',
+        "[W1021 05:04:29.512 ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1250] Warning: destroy_process_group() was not called",
+        "    assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps",
+        "AssertionError",
+    ]
+    body = "".join(f"[rank3]: {line}\n" for line in lines)
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=1)))
+    assert (
+        result["failure_detail"]
+        == "AssertionError: assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps (sched.py:74)"
+    )
+
+
+def test_an_interrupt_with_a_stray_exception_line_keeps_the_signal(tmp_path):
+    body = "[WARNING] ImportError: optional apex missing\n" + _traceback("train", "KeyboardInterrupt")
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(
+        str(
+            write_log(
+                tmp_path, body, exit_code=130 + 13, failure_reason="signal: killed by SIGTERM (exit 143)"
+            )
+        )
+    )
+    assert result["failure_reason"] == "signal"
+
+
+def test_an_interrupt_traceback_leaves_the_runners_verdict(tmp_path):
+    body = _traceback("train", "KeyboardInterrupt")
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(
+        str(write_log(tmp_path, body, exit_code=143, failure_reason="signal: killed by SIGTERM (exit 143)"))
+    )
+    assert result["failure_reason"] == "signal"

+
+def test_exit_zero_without_a_training_step_is_no_metrics(tmp_path):
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(write_log(tmp_path, "training finished\n", failure_reason="none")))
+    assert (result["status"], result["failure_reason"], result["failed_at"]) == ("failed", "no_metrics", None)

+def test_failed_at_tells_setup_from_training(tmp_path):
+    crashed = extract.parse_log_file(
+        str(write_log(tmp_path, MEGATRON_AVG + "RuntimeError: boom\n", exit_code=1, name="a.log"))
+    )
+    hung = extract.parse_log_file(
+        str(
+            write_log(
+                tmp_path,
+                "compiling...\n",
+                exit_code=143,
+                failure_reason="idle: no new output for MAX_IDLE_SECONDS=1200s",
+                name="b.log",
+            )
+        )

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The failing rank's own log
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+failure = extract.failure
+
+
+def torchrun_summary(
+    rank: int, local_rank: int, exitcode: int, time: str, host: str = "node-1.cluster"
+) -> str:
+    return (
+        "Root Cause (first observed failure):\n[0]:\n"
+        f"  time      : {time}\n  host      : {host}\n"
+        f"  rank      : {rank} (local_rank: {local_rank})\n  exitcode  : {exitcode} (pid: 1758)\n"
+        "  error_file: <N/A>\n  traceback : To enable traceback see: https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/elastic/errors.html\n"
+        "============================================================\n"
+    )
+
+
+def test_failing_rank_is_the_earliest_root_cause():
+    lines = (
+        torchrun_summary(9, 1, -15, "2026-10-22_18:53:20", "node-2")
+        + torchrun_summary(3, 3, 1, "2026-10-22_18:53:14", "node-1")
+    ).splitlines(keepends=True)
+    assert failure.failing_rank(lines) == {
+        "rank": 3,
+        "local_rank": 3,
+        "host": "node-1",
+        "exitcode": 1,
+        "time": "2026-10-22_18:53:14",
+    }
+    assert failure.failing_rank(["training...\n"]) is None
+
+
+def rank_record(time: str, level: str, message: str) -> str:
+    """A record of Primus's per-rank log files (no colours)."""
+    return f"[{time}][root/amd][pre_trainer][ip-localhost][rank-3/8]{f'[{level}]':<11}[-----traceback.py:1050] : {message}\n"
+
+
+def failing_rank_run(tmp_path, with_rank_log: bool = True) -> Path:
+    """A log whose rank 3 failed first, with rank 3's error.log in a workspace
+    given through EXTRA_ENV; the log has no section yet."""
+    workspace = tmp_path / "ws"
+    rank_dir = workspace / "amd" / "root" / "exp1" / "logs" / "pre_trainer" / "rank-3"
+    if with_rank_log:
+        rank_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
+        (rank_dir / "error.log").write_text(
+            rank_record("20261021 09:00:00", "ERROR", "ValueError: an earlier run of this experiment")
+            + rank_record(
+                "20261022 18:52:05",
+                "ERROR",
+                "[Patch] ✗ Patch 'x' failed due to missing dependency: no triton",
+            )
+            + "Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
+            + '  File "/primus/core/patches/patch_runner.py", line 127, in run_patches\n'
+            + "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'triton'\n"
+            + rank_record("20261022 18:52:27", "ERROR", "Traceback (most recent call last):")
+            + rank_record("20261022 18:52:27", "ERROR", '  File "/Megatron-LM/x.py", line 74, in __init__')
+            + "    assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps\n"
+            + rank_record("20261022 18:52:27", "ERROR", "AssertionError")
+            + rank_record(
+                "20261022 18:52:27",
+                "ERROR",
+                "[Primus] Error: RuntimeError: Training execution failed:  (x.py:121)",
+            )
+        )
+    body = (
+        primus_record("INFO", "train_runtime.py:90", "starting").replace(
+            "20261021 05:06:54", "20261022 18:52:00"
+        )
+        + "torch.distributed.elastic.multiprocessing.errors.ChildFailedError: \n"
+        + torchrun_summary(3, 3, 1, "2026-10-22_18:52:29")
+    )
+    log = write_log(
+        tmp_path,
+        body,
+        exit_code=1,
+        failure_reason="exit: launcher exited with code 1",
+        with_footer=False,
+        config_body="workspace: ${PRIMUS_WORKSPACE:./output}\nexp_name: ${PRIMUS_EXP_NAME:exp1}\nmodules:\n  pre_trainer:\n    framework: megatron\n",
+        banner_extra=f"# Train Module     : pre_trainer  (CLI verb: train pretrain)\n# Extra env (--env): PRIMUS_WORKSPACE={workspace}\n",
+    )
+    return log
+
+
+def finish_log(log: Path, section: list[str] | None) -> None:
+    """End the log the way the runner does: section, then footer."""
+    footer = FOOTER_TEMPLATE.format(
+        exit_code=1, failure_line="# Failure reason   : exit: launcher exited with code 1\n"
+    )
+    head, _, tail = footer.partition("\n\n")
+    log.write_text(log.read_text() + head + "\n\n" + ("\n".join(section) + "\n\n" if section else "") + tail)
+
+
+def test_the_failing_ranks_own_records_are_the_cause(tmp_path):
+    log = failing_rank_run(tmp_path)
+    spec = failure.failing_rank_spec(str(log), str(tmp_path), since=0)
+    assert (spec["rank"], spec["workspace"], spec["exp_name"], spec["module"]) == (
+        3,
+        str(tmp_path / "ws"),
+        "exp1",
+        "pre_trainer",
+    )
+    section = failure.failing_rank_section(spec)
+    assert section[1] == "# Failing rank     : 3 (local rank 3) on node-1.cluster, exit code 1"
+    assert "an earlier run" not in "\n".join(section)
+    finish_log(log, section)
+
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(log))
+    assert (result["failing_rank"], result["failing_host"]) == (3, "node-1.cluster")
+    assert (result["failure_reason"], result["failure_detail"]) == (
+        "python_error",
+        "AssertionError: assert self.lr_warmup_steps < self.lr_decay_steps (x.py:74)",
+    )
+
+
+def test_a_missing_rank_log_still_names_the_rank(tmp_path):
+    log = failing_rank_run(tmp_path, with_rank_log=False)
+    section = failure.failing_rank_section(failure.failing_rank_spec(str(log), str(tmp_path)))
+    assert section[2].startswith("# Source           : no rank-3 log under")
+    finish_log(log, section)
+    result = extract.parse_log_file(str(log))
+    assert result["failing_rank"] == 3
+    assert result["failure_reason"] == "exit"
+

+def test_a_back_to_back_run_of_the_same_experiment_is_left_out(tmp_path):
+    log = failing_rank_run(tmp_path)
+    error_log = tmp_path / "ws" / "amd" / "root" / "exp1" / "logs" / "pre_trainer" / "rank-3" / "error.log"
+    previous = rank_record("20261022 18:51:50", "ERROR", "ValueError: the previous run's error")
+    error_log.write_text(previous + error_log.read_text())
+    # The run started at 18:51:58 UTC; its first Primus line is at 18:52:00.
+    since = datetime(2026, 10, 22, 18, 51, 58, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp()
+    section = failure.failing_rank_section(failure.failing_rank_spec(str(log), str(tmp_path), since=since))
+    assert "previous run" not in "\n".join(section)
+    assert any("AssertionError" in line for line in section)
+
+
+def test_a_specific_cause_in_rank_0s_output_beats_the_sections(tmp_path):
+    section = [
+        "#### Begin Failing Rank Output ####",
+        "# Failing rank     : 3 (local rank 3) on node-1, exit code 1",
+        f"# Source           : /x/rank-3/error.log ({failure.OWN_RECORDS})",
+        rank_record(
+            "20261022 18:52:27",
+            "ERROR",
+            "RuntimeError: NCCL error in: ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1 ncclSystemError",
+        ).rstrip(),
+        "#### End Failing Rank Output ####",
+    ]
+    log = write_log(
+        tmp_path,
+        "Last RCCL warning: 'Bootstrap : no socket interface found'\n",
+        exit_code=1,
+        with_footer=False,
+    )
+    finish_log(log, section)
+    assert extract.parse_log_file(str(log))["failure_reason"] == "nic_error"
+
+
+def test_the_failing_ranks_exception_beats_the_nccl_errors_it_left_behind(tmp_path):

+            if line.endswith(ANSI_RESET):
+                return start
+            for j in range(start + 1, end):
+                if self.raw[j].rstrip("\r\n").endswith(ANSI_RESET):
+                    return j
+            return start
+        if PATCH_SKIPPED not in line:
+            return start
+        last, j = start, start + 1
+        while j < end and self._clean(j).strip() == TRACEBACK_MARKER:
+            j += 1
+            while j < end and (not self._clean(j).strip() or self._clean(j)[0].isspace()):
+                j += 1
+            last = j  # the exception line
+            j += 1
+            while j < end and (not self._clean(j).strip() or self._clean(j).strip() in CHAIN_LINKS):
+                j += 1
+        return min(last, n - 1)
+
+    def __getitem__(self, i: int) -> str | None:
+        if i in self.noise:
+            return None
+        clean = self._clean(i)
+        if clean.startswith(("[", "(")):
+            m = PRIMUS_RECORD_RE.match(clean) or TORCH_RANK_PREFIX_RE.match(clean)
+            if m:
+                return clean[m.end() :]
+        return clean
+
+    def tag(self, i: int) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
+        """``(rank, level)`` of a Primus record line, None for any other line."""
+        clean = self._clean(i)
+        m = PRIMUS_RECORD_RE.match(clean) if clean.startswith(("[", "(")) else None
+        return (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else None
+
+
+def _read_traceback(texts: _OutputTexts, start: int) -> tuple[dict | None, int]:
+    """The traceback whose header is on line ``start``, and the index after it.
+    The exception is None when the block does not end in an exception line.
+    Indentation counts from the header's, as torchrun's summary indents the
+    traceback it got from a rank's error file. Records of another rank or log
+    level, and torchrun's and the launcher's own lines, are skipped."""
+    frames: list[dict] = []
+    header = texts[start] or ""
+    base = len(header) - len(header.lstrip())
+    owner = texts.tag(start)
+    i = start + 1
+    end = min(len(texts), start + MAX_TRACEBACK_LINES)
+    while i < end:
+        text = texts[i]
+        i += 1
+        if text is None or not text.strip() or CARET_RE.match(text) or FOREIGN_LINE_RE.match(text):
+            continue
+        tag = texts.tag(i - 1)
+        if tag is not None and tag != owner:
+            continue
+        frame = FRAME_RE.match(text)
+        if frame:
+            frames.append({"file": frame.group(1), "line": int(frame.group(2)), "source": None})
+        elif len(text) - len(text.lstrip()) > base:
+            if frames and frames[-1]["source"] is None:
+                frames[-1]["source"] = text.strip()
+        else:
+            m = EXCEPTION_RE.match(text.strip())
+            if not m:
+                return None, i - 1
+            exception = {
+                "type": m.group(1),
+                "message": (m.group(2) or "").strip(),
+                "text": text.strip(),
+                "frames": frames,
+                "index": i - 1,
+            }
+            return exception, i
+    return None, i
+
+
+def _traceback_chains(texts: _OutputTexts) -> list[list[dict]]:
+    """Every traceback in the output, chained as Python prints them: each chain
+    lists its exceptions cause first, and an exception's ``link`` ("cause" or
+    "context") says how it relates to the one before it."""
+    chains: list[list[dict]] = []
+    linkable = False  # an exception was read, so a link line can follow it
+    link = None
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(texts):
+        if TRACEBACK_MARKER in texts.raw[i] and (texts[i] or "").strip().endswith(TRACEBACK_MARKER):
+            exception, i = _read_traceback(texts, i)
+            if exception is None:
+                linkable, link = False, None
+                continue
+            exception["link"] = link
+            if link and chains:
+                chains[-1].append(exception)
+            else:
+                chains.append([exception])
+            linkable, link = True, None
+            continue
+        # The rest of a multi-line exception message may come before the link
+        # line; after it, only blank lines before the next traceback.
+        if linkable:
+            if link is None:
+                if "exception" in texts.raw[i]:
+                    link = CHAIN_LINKS.get((texts[i] or "").strip())
+            elif (texts[i] or "").strip():
+                linkable, link = False, None
+        i += 1
+    return chains
+
+
+def _is_wrapper(exception: dict) -> bool:
+    return exception["type"].endswith(GENERIC_EXCEPTIONS) or exception["text"].startswith(TRAINING_WRAPPER)
+
+
+def _root_exception(chain: list[dict]) -> dict | None:
+    """The exception a chain started from: back along "raise ... from" links and
+    past wrappers. None for a chain of torchrun's summary alone."""
+    i = len(chain) - 1
+    while i > 0 and (chain[i]["link"] == "cause" or _is_wrapper(chain[i])):
+        i -= 1
+    return None if chain[i]["type"].endswith(GENERIC_EXCEPTIONS) else chain[i]
+
+
+def _fatal_exception(texts: _OutputTexts) -> tuple[dict | None, bool]:
+    """The exception that stopped the run: the root of the last chain printed
+    before Primus's first "[Primus] Error:" line, else of the last chain. An
+    earlier traceback is usually one that was caught and logged. Also whether
+    the run was stopped from outside: that chain ends in an interrupt or exit."""
+    chains = _traceback_chains(texts)
+    anchor = next(
+        (
+            i
+            for i, line in enumerate(texts.raw)
+            if PRIMUS_ERROR in line and (texts[i] or "").lstrip().startswith(PRIMUS_ERROR)
+        ),
+        None,
+    )
+    if anchor is not None and any(chain[-1]["index"] < anchor for chain in chains):
+        chains = [chain for chain in chains if chain[-1]["index"] < anchor]
+    for chain in reversed(chains):
+        if chain[-1]["type"].endswith(NOT_A_FAILURE):
+            return None, True
+        root = _root_exception(chain)
+        if root is not None:
+            return root, False
+    return None, False
+
+
+def _exception_detail(exception: dict) -> str:
+    """The exception line. A bare one gets the location of the frame that
+    raised it, and a bare AssertionError the failed assert as well."""
+    text = exception["text"]
+    if not exception["message"] and exception["frames"]:
+        frame = exception["frames"][-1]
+        where = f"{os.path.basename(frame['file'])}:{frame['line']}"
+        if frame["source"] and exception["type"].endswith("AssertionError"):
+            text = f"{exception['type']}: {frame['source']} ({where})"
+        else:
+            text = f"{exception['type']} ({where})"
+    return text[:MAX_DETAIL_CHARS]
+
+
+def _line_owner(texts: _OutputTexts, i: int) -> tuple[str, str] | str | None:
+    """Who wrote line ``i``: a Primus record's ``(rank, level)``, PyTorch's
+    "[rankN]:" prefix, or None for a line with neither."""
+    tag = texts.tag(i)
+    if tag is not None:
+        return tag
+    m = TORCH_RANK_PREFIX_RE.match(texts._clean(i))
+    return m.group(0).strip() if m else None
+
+
+def _nccl_last_error(texts: _OutputTexts, index: int) -> str | None:
+    """The "Last error:" of the NCCL error message on line ``index``. The
+    message goes on in its writer's lines: those with the same "[rankN]:"
+    prefix, else unprefixed ones up to that rank's next record; other ranks'
+    lines in between are skipped."""
+    owner = _line_owner(texts, index)
+    message: list[str] = []
+    for i in range(index + 1, min(len(texts), index + MAX_LAST_ERROR_LINES)):
+        who = _line_owner(texts, i)
+        if isinstance(owner, str):
+            if who != owner:
+                continue
+        elif who is not None:
+            if isinstance(who, tuple) and isinstance(owner, tuple) and who[0] == owner[0]:
+                break
+            continue
+        text = (texts[i] or "").strip()
+        if text == TRACEBACK_MARKER or text in CHAIN_LINKS or FOREIGN_LINE_RE.match(text):
+            break
+        message.append(text)
+    for j, text in enumerate(message):
+        if not text.startswith(NCCL_LAST_ERROR):
+            continue
+        rest = text[len(NCCL_LAST_ERROR) :].strip()
+        if rest:
+            return rest
+        following = next((t for t in message[j + 1 :] if t), None)
+        if following and not following.startswith((PRIMUS_ERROR, "Exception raised from")):
+            return following
+        return None
+    return None
+
+
+def _with_last_error(detail: str, texts: _OutputTexts, index: int) -> str:
+    """``detail`` with NCCL's last error, which says what failed, kept within
+    MAX_DETAIL_CHARS."""
+    last_error = _nccl_last_error(texts, index)
+    if not last_error:
+        return detail
+    detail = NCCL_LOCATION_RE.sub(":", detail, count=1).replace(NCCL_DEBUG_HINT, "")
+    suffix = f" | {NCCL_LAST_ERROR} {strip_ansi(last_error).strip()}"
+    room = max(MAX_DETAIL_CHARS // 2, MAX_DETAIL_CHARS - len(suffix))
+    return (detail[:room] + suffix)[:MAX_DETAIL_CHARS]
+
+
+def _fatal_detail(texts: _OutputTexts, fatal: dict) -> str:
+    detail = _exception_detail(fatal)
+    return _with_last_error(detail, texts, fatal["index"]) if NCCL_ERROR_RE.search(fatal["text"]) else detail
+
+
+def scan_failure_text(run_lines: list[str]) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
+    texts = _OutputTexts(run_lines)
+    first: dict[str, str] = {}
+    first_index: dict[str, int] = {}
+    oom_lines: list[str] = []
+    gpu_fault = False
+    traceback_seen = False
+    tail_exception = None  # last exception line after a traceback header
+    loose_exception = None  # first "XError: ..." anywhere
+    for i, line in enumerate(run_lines):
+        if not FAILURE_PREFILTER_RE.search(line.lower()):
+            continue
+        text = texts[i]
+        if text is None:
+            continue
+        for category, pattern in FAILURE_PATTERNS:
+            if pattern.search(text):
+                first.setdefault(category, text)
+                first_index.setdefault(category, i)
+                if category == "oom":
+                    oom_lines.append(text)
+        if not gpu_fault and GPU_FAULT_RE.search(text):
+            gpu_fault = True
+        if TRACEBACK_MARKER in text:
+            traceback_seen = True
+        elif traceback_seen:
+            m = PY_EXCEPTION_LINE_RE.match(text.strip())
+            if m and not m.group(1).endswith(GENERIC_EXCEPTIONS):
+                tail_exception = text
+        if loose_exception is None:
+            m = PY_EXCEPTION_RE.search(text)
+            if m and not m.group(1).endswith(GENERIC_EXCEPTIONS):
+                loose_exception = text[m.start() :]
+    if gpu_fault and oom_lines and all(RCCL_ALLOC_RE.search(line) for line in oom_lines):
+        del first["oom"]
+    for category in ("nic_error", "oom", "segfault"):
+        if category not in first:
+            continue
+        if category == "oom" and _oom_is_contended(oom_lines):
+            return "gpu_contended", clean_detail(next(l for l in oom_lines if OOM_TOTAL_RE.search(l)))
+        return category, clean_detail(first[category])
+    fatal, stopped = _fatal_exception(texts)
+    if "nccl_error" in first:
+        if fatal is not None and NCCL_ERROR_RE.search(fatal["text"]):
+            return "nccl_error", _fatal_detail(texts, fatal)
+        return "nccl_error", _with_last_error(
+            clean_detail(first["nccl_error"]), texts, first_index["nccl_error"]
+        )
+    if fatal is not None:
+        return "python_error", _fatal_detail(texts, fatal)
+    # Stopped by a signal or an exit call: an exception line elsewhere is not why.
+    for exception in () if stopped else (tail_exception, loose_exception):
+        if exception:
+            return "python_error", clean_detail(exception)
+    return None, None
+
+
+def fatal_exception_detail(lines: list[str]) -> str | None:
+    """The detail scan_failure_text gives the exception that stopped the run,
+    when ``lines`` hold one in a traceback it could read."""
+    texts = _OutputTexts(lines)
+    fatal, _ = _fatal_exception(texts)
+    return _fatal_detail(texts, fatal) if fatal is not None else None
+
+
+def last_output_line(run_lines: list[str]) -> str | None:
+    for line in reversed(run_lines):
+        text = clean_detail(line)
+        if text and not text.startswith(">>>"):
+            return text
+    return None
+
+
+def legacy_footer_reason(footer: dict, run_lines: list[str], exit_code: int | None) -> str | None:
+    """Rebuild a ``Failure reason`` for logs written before the footer had one.
+
+    Older single-node runners wrote exit 130 on Ctrl+C; the older multi-node
+    runner marked watchdog kills with ``Failure pattern? : true`` and a
+    ``>>> ... TIMEOUT`` line, whatever the exit code.
+    """
+    if footer.get("failure_pattern_flag") == "true":
+        if any(">>>" in line and "TIMEOUT" in line for line in run_lines[-200:]):
+            return "timeout: stopped by the older runner's MAX_RUN_SECONDS"
+        return "fail_pattern: failure text matched the older runner's FAIL_PATTERN"
+    if exit_code is None or exit_code == 0:
+        return None
+    if exit_code == 130:
+        return "interrupted: exit 130 from an older runner"
+    if 128 < exit_code < 160:
+        try:
+            name = signal.Signals(exit_code - 128).name
+        except ValueError:
+            name = f"signal {exit_code - 128}"
+        return f"signal: killed by {name} (exit {exit_code})"
+    return f"exit: launcher exited with code {exit_code}"
+
+
+def classify_failure(
+    run_lines: list[str],
+    footer_reason: str | None,
+    exit_code: int | None,
+    rank_lines: list[str] | None = None,
+) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
+    """Return ``(failure_reason, failure_detail)`` for a run that did not pass.
+
+    The runner's own verdict wins when it is definitive (it stopped a hang,
+    or the batch was interrupted). Otherwise the cause in the failing rank's
+    own log (``rank_lines``, see failing_rank_output), then in the output, is
+    more useful than the bare exit status, which comes last. A failed run
+    always gets a reason, ``unknown`` at worst.
+    """
+    footer_cat, _, footer_detail = (footer_reason or "").partition(":")
+    footer_cat = footer_cat.strip()
+    footer_detail = footer_detail.strip() or None
+
+    # "steps": the diffusion_dlrm run listing the diffusion_bench steps that
+    # failed; "not_run": a config the runner did not launch, and why.
+    if footer_cat in ("timeout", "idle", "interrupted", "steps", "not_run"):
+        return footer_cat, footer_detail
+    rank = scan_failure_text(rank_lines) if rank_lines else (None, None)
+    output = scan_failure_text(run_lines)
+    # Only a specific cause in the output outranks the failing rank's own: the
+    # NCCL errors of the ranks it left behind are what the output usually has.
+    if output[0] in SPECIFIC_REASONS and (
+        rank[0] not in SPECIFIC_REASONS or SPECIFIC_REASONS.index(output[0]) < SPECIFIC_REASONS.index(rank[0])
+    ):
+        return output
+    for text_cat, text_detail in (rank, output):
+        if text_cat:
+            return text_cat, text_detail
+    if footer_cat == "signal":
+        return ("killed" if "SIGKILL" in (footer_detail or "") else "signal"), footer_detail
+    if footer_cat in ("fail_pattern", "exit"):
+        return footer_cat, last_output_line(run_lines) or footer_detail
+    return "unknown", last_output_line(run_lines)
+
+
+def settle_outcome(result: dict, iterations: list[dict]) -> None:
+    """What only the parsed steps of a training run tell: a run that exited 0
+    without logging a step failed (no_metrics), and how far a run that did not
+    pass got. A no_metrics run finished, so it has no failed_at."""
+    if result["status"] == "ok" and not iterations:
+        result["status"] = "failed"
+        result["failure_reason"] = "no_metrics"
+        result["failure_detail"] = "the run exited 0 but logged no training step"
+    elif (
+        result["status"] in ("failed", "interrupted", "incomplete") and result["failure_reason"] != "not_run"
+    ):
+        result["failed_at"] = (
+            f"after step {max(it.get('step', 0) for it in iterations)}" if iterations else "setup"
+        )
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The failing rank's own log
+#
+# For the PyTorch backends the console shows local rank 0 only (and the last
+# local rank of the last node), so when another rank fails first, its error is
+# not in the run log. torchrun's summary names that rank ("Root Cause (first
+# observed failure)"), and Primus writes every rank's ERROR records to
+# <workspace>/<team>/<user>/<exp>/logs/<module>/rank-<N>/error.log. After a
+# failed run, the runner copies that rank's records from this run into the
+# log, between "End Run Output" and the footer.
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ROOT_CAUSE_MARKER = "Root Cause (first observed failure):"
+SUMMARY_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(time|host|rank|exitcode)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*$")
+SUMMARY_RANK_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d+)(?:\s*\(local_rank:\s*(\d+)\))?")
+PRIMUS_TIMESTAMP_RE = re.compile(r"^\[(\d{8} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\]")
+PRIMUS_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT = "%Y%m%d %H:%M:%S"
+PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"^\$\{([^:}]+):([^}]*)\}$")
+# Of the runner's own environment, these reach the container without EXTRA_ENV.
+FORWARDED_PREFIXES = ("PRIMUS_",)
+FAILING_RANK_BEGIN = "Begin Failing Rank Output"
+FAILING_RANK_END = "End Failing Rank Output"
+FAILING_RANK_FIELD_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^# Failing rank\s*:\s*(\d+)(?: \(local rank (\d+)\))?(?: on ([^\s,]+))?(?:, exit code (-?\d+))?"
+)
+MAX_SECTION_LINES = 200
+MAX_TAIL_BYTES = 4 << 20
+# Before the run's start, for other nodes' clocks; a run of the same
+# experiment just before this one is further back than that.
+CLOCK_SLACK = timedelta(seconds=5)
+OWN_RECORDS = "its ERROR records from this run"
+# Most specific first. Of the run output's reasons, only these outrank the
+# failing rank's own.
+SPECIFIC_REASONS = ("nic_error", "oom", "gpu_contended", "segfault")
+
+
+def failing_rank(run_lines: list[str]) -> dict | None:
+    """The rank torchrun's summary names as the first to fail, as
+    ``{"rank", "local_rank", "host", "exitcode", "time"}``: the earliest when
+    several nodes print one. None when there is no summary."""
+    found = []
+    for i, line in enumerate(run_lines):
+        if ROOT_CAUSE_MARKER not in line:
+            continue
+        fields: dict[str, str] = {}
+        for follow in run_lines[i + 1 : i + 12]:
+            clean = strip_ansi(follow)
+            if clean.startswith("====="):
+                break
+            m = SUMMARY_FIELD_RE.match(clean)
+            if m:
+                fields.setdefault(m.group(1), m.group(2))
+        rank = SUMMARY_RANK_RE.match(fields.get("rank", ""))
+        if not rank:
+            continue
+        code = re.match(r"-?\d+", fields.get("exitcode", ""))
+        found.append(
+            {
+                "rank": int(rank.group(1)),
+                "local_rank": int(rank.group(2)) if rank.group(2) else None,
+                "host": fields.get("host") or None,
+                "exitcode": int(code.group(0)) if code else None,
+                "time": fields.get("time", ""),
+            }
+        )
+    if not found:
+        return None
+    # torchrun stops the other ranks with a signal (a negative exit code).
+    return min(found, key=lambda f: (f["time"], (f["exitcode"] or 0) < 0))
+
+
+def _between(lines: list[str], begin: str, end: str) -> list[str]:
+    start = next((i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if begin in line), None)
+    if start is None:
+        return []
+    stop = next((i for i in range(start + 1, len(lines)) if end in lines[i]), len(lines))
+    return lines[start + 1 : stop]
+
+
+def _resolve(value: str, env: dict[str, str]) -> str:
+    """A config value with its ``${VAR:default}`` placeholder resolved."""
+    value = value.strip().strip("'\"")
+    m = PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(value)
+    return (env.get(m.group(1)) or m.group(2)) if m else value
+
+
+def failing_rank_spec(log_path: str, primus_path: str, since: float = 0) -> dict | None:
+    """Where to look for the failing rank's log of the run in ``log_path``,
+    with the rank as failing_rank gives it; None when torchrun named none.
+    ``since`` is the run's start (epoch seconds, the runner's clock)."""
+    with open(log_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
+        lines = f.readlines()
+    run_lines = _between(lines, "Begin Run Output", "End Run Output") or lines
+    who = failing_rank(run_lines)
+    if who is None:
+        return None
+    banner: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for line in lines:
+        if "Begin Config File Dump" in line:
+            break
+        m = re.match(r"^#\s*([^:]+?)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*$", line)
+        if m:
+            banner.setdefault(m.group(1), m.group(2))
+    config = "".join(_between(lines, "Begin Config File Dump", "End Config File Dump"))
+
+    # The container's view: EXTRA_ENV, then the runner's forwarded variables.
+    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k.startswith(FORWARDED_PREFIXES)}
+    extra = banner.get("Extra env (--env)", "")
+    if extra and extra != "<none>":
+        for token in shlex.split(extra):
+            key, sep, value = token.partition("=")
+            if sep:
+                env[key] = value
+
+    def top_level(key: str, default: str) -> str:
+        m = re.search(rf"^{key}:\s*(.+?)\s*$", config, re.MULTILINE)
+        return _resolve(m.group(1), env) if m else default
+
+    workspace = top_level("workspace", "./output")
+    if not os.path.isabs(workspace):
+        workspace = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(primus_path, workspace))
+    first = next((m.group(1) for m in map(PRIMUS_TIMESTAMP_RE.match, map(strip_ansi, run_lines)) if m), None)
+    return {
+        **who,
+        "workspace": workspace,
+        "exp_name": top_level("exp_name", ""),
+        "module": (banner.get("Train Module") or "").split(" ")[0],
+        "since": since,
+        "window_start": first,
+    }
+
+
+def _find_rank_dir(spec: dict) -> str | None:
+    """The directory of the rank's logs for this run's experiment, written to
+    during the run; any experiment's only when the run's is not known."""
+    rank = f"rank-{spec['rank']}"
+    exp = glob.escape(spec["exp_name"]) if spec.get("exp_name") else "*"
+    module = glob.escape(spec["module"]) if spec.get("module") else "*"
+    since = float(spec.get("since") or 0) - CLOCK_SLACK.total_seconds()
+
+    def written(path: str) -> float:
+        files = [os.path.join(path, name) for name in ("error.log", "debug.log")]
+        return max((os.path.getmtime(f) for f in files if os.path.isfile(f)), default=0)
+
+    for pattern in ((exp, module), (exp, "*")):
+        dirs = [
+            d
+            for d in glob.glob(
+                os.path.join(spec["workspace"], "*", "*", pattern[0], "logs", pattern[1], rank)
+            )
+        ]
+        dirs = [d for d in dirs if written(d) >= since]
+        if dirs:
+            return max(dirs, key=written)
+    return None
+
+
+def _run_cut(spec: dict) -> str | None:
+    """The time of this run's first possible record, in the container's clock
+    as Primus writes it: the run's start (epoch seconds) moved by the
